standards.name: MINiML (MIAME Notation in Markup Language)
standards.abstract: MINiML is an XML-based data exchange format developed and maintained by NCBI GEO for representing microarray gene expression and other high-throughput molecular abundance data. It models basic relations between Platform (array), Sample (hybridization), and Series (experiment) and captures the elements of the MIAME checklist while allowing additional submitter-provided information. MINiML provides an XML Schema (XSD) with element definitions, constraints and controlled vocabularies to ensure structured submissions and interoperable metadata for GEO.

classification.rationale: The source provides an explicit 'Elements and Content Guidelines' table that lists element names, multiplicity, allowed values/constraints and content guidance (e.g., 'Title required string of length 1-120 characters...'), i.e. named metadata fields with concrete types/constraints rather than prose reporting instructions. Quote: "The table below provides content guidelines and constraints for most MINiML elements; it is not exhaustive."

standards.name: GEO Platform content guidelines — Platform table headers (SOFT / Platform table)
standards.abstract: This standard covers the tab-delimited Platform table used by the NCBI Gene Expression Omnibus (GEO) to describe array/sequencer feature lists (e.g., oligos, clones, PCR products) that define a Platform (GPL) record. The research objects are array features or sequence-derived features on high-throughput functional genomics platforms; submitters provide a header row plus one row per feature, and the recording modality is a tab-delimited table of identifiers and annotations that reference sequences or coordinates. The guidelines are maintained by NCBI/NCBI GEO and are intended to ensure Platform tables contain meaningful, trackable sequence identifiers and a required ID column so datasets are interpretable and linkable to Sample and Series records; the page lists specific standard column headers (ID, SEQUENCE, GB_ACC, GB_LIST, GB_RANGE, RANGE_GB, RANGE_START, RANGE_END, RANGE_STRAND, etc.) and describes expected content/format for each.

classification.rationale: The source presents a genuine table of standard column headers (a header name and explicit content/format guidance for each), i.e., named fields with concrete expected formats/types rather than prose checklists or procedural steps. Each listed header is an independently meaningful data column (ID, SEQUENCE, GB_ACC, GB_RANGE, RANGE_START, etc.), so the material is best represented as a MetadataTable.

ID.name: ID
ID.descr: Unique identifier for each row/feature in the Platform table; corresponds to ID_REF in Sample tables and must appear first.
ID.evidence: (Required) An identifier that unambiguously identifies each row on your Platform table. Each ID within a Platform table must be unique. This column heading should appear first and may be used only once in the data table. Keep in mind that the ID column you provide in your Platform data table corresponds with the ID_REF column you provide in accompanying Sample data tables. Sample data tables should contain normalized data. If your normalization strategy requires taking the average of replicate array features, your Platform should reflect the condensed template. In this case, please e-mail or FTP the full template file to us and we will attach it to your Platform record as a supplementary file.

raw_full_info.uniqueness: IDs must be unique within the Platform table
raw_full_info.relation: corresponds to ID_REF in Sample tables

SEQUENCE.name: SEQUENCE
SEQUENCE.descr: The nucleotide sequence of the oligo/clone/PCR product represented by the feature.
SEQUENCE.evidence: The nucleotide sequence of each oligo, clone or PCR product.

GB_ACC.name: GB_ACC
GB_ACC.descr: GenBank or RefSeq accession on which the feature/sequence is based; include version numbers when possible.
GB_ACC.evidence: GenBank accession - identifies a biological sequence through the GenBank sequence accession number assigned to the sequence, or the representative GenBank or RefSeq accession number upon which your sequence was designed. It is recommended that you include the version number of the accessions upon which your sequences were designed (e.g., NM_022975.1 rather than NM_022975). This is particularly important for RefSeq accessions which are updated frequently. GenBank accessions representing the top BLAST hits for your sequences are not acceptable. Also, chromosome, genome and contig accession numbers are generally not acceptable as they are not specific enough to accurately identify the portion of the sequence printed on arrays (use GB_RANGE instead).

raw_full_info.expected: GenBank or RefSeq accession (include version number when available)
raw_full_info.notes: Top BLAST hits and chromosome/genome/contig accessions generally not acceptable; use GB_RANGE for positional specification

GB_LIST.name: GB_LIST
GB_LIST.descr: List of GenBank accession numbers (multiple accessions allowed), e.g., representing different clone ends.
GB_LIST.evidence: GenBank accession list - as for GB_ACC, but allows more than one GenBank accession number to be presented. For example, your sequences may have GenBank accession numbers representing both the 5' and 3' ends of your clones. Multiple accession numbers should be separated using commas or spaces. Alternatively, more than one GB_ACC column may be supplied.

raw_full_info.format: multiple accession numbers separated by commas or spaces
raw_full_info.alternative: multiple GB_ACC columns may be supplied instead

GB_RANGE.name: GB_RANGE
GB_RANGE.descr: GenBank accession range that specifies a particular sequence position within an accession (useful for tiling arrays).
GB_RANGE.evidence: GenBank accession range - specifies a particular sequence position within a GenBank accession number. Use format ACCESSION.VERSION[start..end]. Useful for tiling arrays.

RANGE_GB.name: RANGE_GB
RANGE_GB.descr: GenBank accession (base) used together with RANGE_START and RANGE_END to specify tiled positions; use ACCESSION.VERSION format.
RANGE_GB.evidence: Use format ACCESSION.VERSION. Should be used in conjunction with RANGE_START and RANGE_END. Useful for tiling arrays.

RANGE_START.name: RANGE_START
RANGE_START.descr: Start coordinate (relative to the RANGE_GB accession) indicating the beginning position of the feature.
RANGE_START.evidence: Use in conjunction with RANGE_GB. Indicates the start position (relative to the RANGE_GB accession). Useful for tiling arrays.

RANGE_END.name: RANGE_END
RANGE_END.descr: End coordinate (relative to the RANGE_GB accession) indicating the ending position of the feature.
RANGE_END.evidence: Use in conjunction with RANGE_GB. Indicates the end position (relative to the RANGE_GB accession). Useful for tiling arrays.

RANGE_STRAND.name: RANGE_STRAND
RANGE_STRAND.descr: Strand indicator for the RANGE_GB coordinates (strand represented).
RANGE_STRAND.evidence: Use in conjunction with RANGE_GB. Indicates the strand represented. Use + o

raw_full_info.notes: source text truncated after 'Use + o' but intent is to indicate '+' or '-' strand

standards.notes: The source page also states overall table-level rules such as 'The first row in the Platform table must be a header line that identifies the content of each column' and that at least one standard column (other than ID) is expected. The Platform table must contain only array-design related information (no expression measurements), and sequence identifiers must be meaningful/trackable (GenBank/RefSeq accessions, locus tags, oligo sequences, chromosome locations, etc.). Evidence for these statements is present on the source page.

standards.name: MIAME (Minimum Information About a Microarray Experiment)
standards.abstract: MIAME (Minimum Information About a Microarray Experiment) specifies the minimum information that should be provided when describing microarray (and analogous high-throughput) studies so that results can be interpreted and reproduced. It covers what to report about raw assay data, processed/normalized results, sample annotation (biological variables and experimental factors), experiment design (sample relationships and replicates), array/feature annotation, and essential laboratory and data-processing protocols. The guidelines were developed by the MGED Consortium and are widely adopted by repositories and journals; GEO provides submission procedures and an explicit metadata template that follow MIAME conventions.

classification.rationale: The source materials include an explicit, column-oriented metadata template (Excel sheet) with named fields/columns for STUDY, SAMPLES, PROTOCOLS, paired-end file columns, and more. This is genuine field-level structure (concrete column names and file columns), so the standard should be represented as a MetadataTable rather than as prose principles or a DAG.

standards.name: NCBI Taxonomy nomenclature
standards.abstract: The NCBI Taxonomy resource is a curated classification and nomenclature for organisms represented in public sequence databases; the primary research object is taxonomic records for organisms (as represented in sequences), accessed and used via a web database and associated tools. The standard/page is provided by the National Center for Biotechnology Information (NCBI) / National Library of Medicine and documents the purpose, scope, and resources of the Taxonomy Database: it defines the curated classification and names, notes its coverage (approximately 10% of described species), lists user guides and tools (Quick Start Guide, FAQ, Handbook, browser, Common Tree, etc.), and publishes important updates and integration links to other NCBI resources. The page functions as descriptive guidance and an index to documentation and tools rather than a field-level metadata schema or a stepwise protocol.

classification.rationale: The source is primarily prose with descriptive statements, headings, and lists of resources/tools/updates — i.e., guidance and documentation items (instructions and descriptions). It does not present a rows-and-columns metadata table nor a sequential DAG of stages, so 'principle' best matches its structure.

principles.principle: Purpose: The Taxonomy Database provides a curated classification and nomenclature for organisms in public sequence databases.
principles.evidence: The Taxonomy Database is a curated classification and nomenclature for all of the organisms in the public sequence databases.

principles.principle: Scope/Coverage: The database currently represents approximately 10% of described species.
principles.evidence: This currently represents about 10% of the described species of life on the planet.

principles.principle: Documentation and guidance: The site provides user-facing documentation and guides (e.g., Quick Start Guide, FAQ, Handbook, FTP).
principles.evidence: Using Taxonomy Quick Start Guide FAQ Handbook Taxonomy FTP

principles.principle: Announcements/Updates: The resource publishes important updates about taxonomy such as changes to phyla, flu species names, and rank changes.
principles.evidence: Important Update: Phyla Changing Important Update: New Flu species Names Important Update: New ranks replaced superkingdom

principles.principle: Tools: The Taxonomy resource offers tools for browsing and analysing taxonomy (Browser, Common Tree, Statistics, Name/ID Status, Genetic Codes, Linking to Taxonomy, Extinct Organisms).
principles.evidence: Taxonomy Tools Browser Common Tree Statistics Name/ID Status Genetic Codes Linking to Taxonomy Extinct Organisms

principles.principle: Integration: The Taxonomy resource links to and integrates with other NCBI resources (GenBank, LinkOut, E-Utilities, Batch Entrez, INSDC, etc.).
principles.evidence: Other Resources GenBank LinkOut E-Utilities Batch Entrez INSDC
